key_insight: Flexible modular robots can move and manipulate objects within the same unit, then physically connect into task-adaptive forms. Together, they can carry objects, cross gaps and navigate difficult terrain.
problem_solved: Fixed robot bodies can limit versatility across tasks. This work addresses how robotic units can adapt their collective physical form to meet different mobility and manipulation demands.
method: Use flexible, tensegrity-based continuum robot modules that combine locomotion and manipulation.
Physically connect modules into cooperative configurations suited to the task.
Apply these configurations to object transport, gap crossing and challenging-terrain navigation.
impact: For embodied AI and robotics practitioners, the work highlights physical reconfiguration as a way to expand robot capabilities. It offers a platform for studying how body design and cooperative behaviour can complement control strategies.
visual_elements: Annotated robot module showing its flexible tensegrity structure and movement capabilities.
Sequence illustrating individual modules connecting into different task-adaptive forms.
Three task panels: carrying an object, crossing a gap and navigating uneven terrain.
Side-by-side comparison of a single module and a connected team performing cooperative tasks.
paper_title: Tensegrity continuum robots enable task-adaptive morphologies for cooperative behaviours
paper_authors: Mahmud Hasan Saikot, Sydney Spiegel, Sudheera Akalanka Kariyawasam, Andrew Stefka, Josh Chrisler
